scope: Literal field correspondence only; independent semantic review pending

items.reason: A scalar count is the consumed information; transferring reservation objects adds data this response never uses. Because reservation details are never opened here, the row can show its count without transferring child records.
items.prompt: In fleet charging coordinator, The capacity screen lists 40 stations and shows each station’s active reservation count. The operator never opens reservation records from this screen. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The list needs counts only, not reservation objects.
The operator never opens reservation records from the capacity screen.

items.reason: The page boundary limits which gardener records belong to the response; loading the whole garden ignores that scope. Only gardeners associated with the returned plot page are needed to build these rows.
items.prompt: In community garden allocation tool, A weekly plot list displays gardener names for 200 plots. The gardener name is required on every row; the page must stay at 25 plots per request. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The page is limited to 25 plot rows but needs the gardener name on each row.
The page contains at most 25 plots.

items.reason: Counts and latest times are aggregates, so annotation entities do not contribute fields the report needs. The returned report consists of two measures rather than annotation content.
items.prompt: In podcast production desk, An archive report needs the number of annotations per episode and the latest annotation time. It does not display annotation text or author profiles. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The report consumes two aggregates, not annotation entities.
The report does not display annotation text or author profiles.

items.reason: The serializer runs after the bounded transaction, so a deferred name read cannot satisfy the export. Each export row must already include the approver name at transaction close.
items.prompt: In permissions review service, An audit export loads grant rows inside a bounded read transaction. Each exported row includes the approver’s display name; no later code runs after the transaction closes. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The export needs the approver name, and deferred reads would occur after the transaction closes.
No application code runs after the export transaction ends.

items.reason: The selected view consumes the complete but explicitly capped grant set during one request. The twelve-row cap makes the complete grant detail part of this selected-principal response.
items.prompt: In digital rights clearance tool, A title detail screen always shows the title, its current territory grants, and each grant expiry. The set is capped at 12 rows and is read in one short request. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: Every current grant and expiry is displayed, and the child set has a small stated cap.
The current grant set is capped at 12 rows.

items.reason: The large notes belong to a later user action and should not burden the fleet summary. Opening a particular aircraft is the only action that consumes its large service notes.
items.prompt: In drone maintenance planner, A weekly fleet report shows aircraft ID and the next battery replacement date. Battery service notes are large and opened only after an operator selects one aircraft. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The report uses a date, while the large notes are a separate selected-aircraft detail.
Service notes are large and opened only for a selected aircraft.

items.reason: Capacity is the only related value this directory consumes; patient records add unrelated data. The directory can display capacity without fetching patient-side relationships.
items.prompt: In clinic referral coordinator, A specialist directory lists 80 clinics. Each clinic row needs its current capacity value, but patient referrals and medical notes must not be fetched on this screen. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: Capacity is the only required related value; patient data is outside this screen.
Patient referrals and notes are outside this directory screen.

items.reason: Thirty separate owner reads would exceed the endpoint’s stated two-read budget. The thirty owner values fit in the one related-data read allowed after the meter page.
items.prompt: In neighborhood energy-sharing service, A dashboard lists 30 meters with the next reserved window. It also shows each meter’s current owner name. The owner table is shared, and the dashboard refreshes once per request. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: Only 30 meter rows and one current owner name per row are needed.
This dashboard endpoint permits at most two database reads per request: the meter page and one related-data read.

items.reason: A per-assignment query makes the number of reads grow with page rows, contrary to the request cap. The shift page can return its row labels without increasing reads as assignments are added.
items.prompt: In volunteer coordination hub, A shift page shows assignments for one shift and the volunteers’ skill labels. Each page contains at most 20 assignments; there is no filtering by skill. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The skill labels are needed for all rows, but the root page is bounded.
This page contract permits at most two database reads, regardless of its 20-row maximum.

items.reason: The list and detail consume different amounts of data; fetching a megabyte log for each list row has no caller benefit. Experiment ID and dataset revision identify a list row; the execution log belongs to result detail.
items.prompt: In research-notebook platform, A result list displays experiment ID and dataset revision. Opening a result shows code commit and execution log. The log may be several megabytes. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The list needs only IDs and dataset revision; the large log belongs to selected detail.
The execution log may be several megabytes.

items.reason: The decision uses the evidence before the bounded read scope ends, so deferred access is too late. The inspector has the selected return evidence while deciding, before leaving the read scope.
items.prompt: In returns inspection workflow, An inspector views one return and always needs its inspection photos and classification history. The screen submits a decision before the read scope ends. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: This workflow uses all of one selected return’s bounded evidence before completing its decision.
The decision is submitted before the read scope ends.

items.reason: The search response does not need the body that a separate page displays. Notice text is absent from search and is fetched only on the separate notice page.
items.prompt: In public-transit disruption board, An operator search returns route and service-day matches. The display needs notice ID, effective time, and platform only; notice text is opened on a separate page. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The search result consumes only three fields and opens text separately.
Notice text is opened on a separate page.

items.reason: Current metadata is sufficient for this edit; historical renditions are not part of the form. The edit uses current descriptive values; no historical rendition is displayed or changed.
items.prompt: In photo-archive curation tool, An archivist edits one asset’s descriptive values while preserving stable asset identity. The edit form shows the asset and current metadata but does not display every historical rendition. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The edit uses current metadata; rendition history is a separate optional view.
The edit form does not display historical renditions.

items.reason: The detail request shows a bounded set for one principal; unrelated grants and principals do not affect it. The response contains active grant expiries for one selected principal within its two-read budget.
items.prompt: In permissions review service, A principal detail view needs active role grants and their expiry dates, but only for the selected principal and at most 10 active grants. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The selected principal has a bounded active-grant set and every expiry is displayed.
This detail request permits at most two database reads for the selected principal.

items.reason: A catalog summary can answer search without loading components the user has not opened. Component detail becomes relevant only after the user opens one bundle.
items.prompt: In subscription packaging service, A catalog search returns bundles with component count and current price. Components are shown only after a bundle is opened. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The search shows a summary; component detail is a separate user action.
Components are shown only after a bundle is opened.

items.reason: Revision metadata answers the search; the binary is needed only for a selected row. Revision number and seal time identify each result row before any binary download.
items.prompt: In document notarization service, A notary searches sealed revisions by document ID and displays each immutable revision number and seal time. The binary document is downloaded only after a row is selected. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The list uses metadata, and bytes are fetched only for the selected immutable revision.
The binary document is downloaded after a row is selected.

items.reason: Totals are the dashboard output; individual payout rows are only needed in seller detail. The dashboard can report settlement-window totals without materializing seller payout details.
items.prompt: In marketplace payout service, The payout dashboard lists seller totals by settlement window. Opening a seller shows the individual payout rows; the dashboard does not need order details. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The summary needs totals, while row details are only used after seller selection.
Order details are not displayed on the dashboard.

items.reason: The operation needs a bounded recent page and current balance; older allocations have a separate search path. The recent allocation page and balance support this account operation while lifetime history stays separate.
items.prompt: In cooperative lending ledger, A repayment screen opens one account, displays its current balance and 12 recent allocations, and can record a new allocation before leaving the account transaction. Older allocations are available through a separate history search. Which read plan fits this caller?
constraints: The operation needs one account and a bounded recent page; historical search is separate.
Older allocations are available through a separate history search.
